A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Layer-wise Feedback Propagation research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the expanded title and substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, SNN training, fine-tuning, and pruning experiments, with additional reward-function and network-depth results in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic-data, image-classification, sparsity, pruning, and SNN experiments, including additional results throughout Appendix A.

M1.justification: The basic LFP updates are retained, but v2 adds BatchNorm parameter/reward rules and skip-connection handling in Sections 3.1.3–3.1.4. It changes the standard classification reward from sigmoid-based to softmax-based, revises the SNN reward, and removes v1's LFP-αβ and LFP-z+z− variants.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR100, CUB, ISIC2019, and Food-11 while retaining CIFAR10 and MNIST coverage. Its two-dimensional blob, circle, and swirl tasks replace v1's one-dimensional sign-classification toy. The 20-class ImageNet evaluation is removed, although ImageNet remains a pretraining source.

E2.justification: Gradient descent remains the principal comparator. In the SNN comparison, v1's surrogate-enabled 'Grad' is retained as 'Surr. + Grad'; v2 adds ordinary gradient descent as a separate control and drops LFP-z+z− from that comparison (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 7).

E3.justification: V1 Appendix A.6.3 specifies Adam for SNNs; v2 Appendix A.6.4 specifies SGD with a one-cycle schedule, a broader learning-rate search, and spike-rate rather than spike-count cross-entropy. V2 also introduces substantial new training and pruning protocols, including BatchNorm canonization, convolution-only pruning, and weighted accuracy for ISIC2019 pruning results.

E4.justification: V2 adds activation-function sweeps, parameter-space update trajectories, and extensive sparsity/pruning analyses using Gini coefficients and relevance-based pruning. V1's rule/composite comparisons, gradient-shattering and depth tests, and gradient-to-LFP fine-tuning study are removed. The simple-reward and SNN hyperparameter studies are reworked.

E5.justification: V1 already reports averages over three or five seeds and depth-study quartiles. V2 explicitly reports mean ± standard deviation in Table 3, identifies standard-deviation shading in several figures, and documents seed initialization. Its toy studies average five dataset draws, while SNN experiments retain three seeds; this does not establish a general increase in runs.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. For example, v2 Table 3 newly reports CUB/VGG-16/ELU accuracy of 0.5 ± 0.0% for LFP versus 69.9 ± 0.4% for gradient descent. V2 adds broader pruning results and revised SNN curves, while removing v1's ImageNet-subset and fine-tuning results. Changed settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix A.2 are substantially replaced. V1 uses a sigmoid-specific, nonnegative-logit convergence argument based on sign agreement and a Taylor approximation. V2 derives exact weight-scaled gradient equivalence by induction for differentiable losses with ReLU hidden layers and linear outputs, changing the formal statement, assumptions, and proof.

C1.justification: V2 adds an explicit claim of computational complexity comparable to gradient descent and makes naturally sparse, easily prunable models a central contribution. V1's contribution framing around efficient transfer learning and extending multiple LRP rules is dropped. The central LFP principle and approximation-free SNN application remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains sparsity through implicit weight scaling and distinguishes genuine prunability from weight-magnitude/importance alignment. Sections 3.4, 4.1, and 5.1 add activation-sign requirements, Heaviside/Sigmoid failure explanations, BatchNorm caveats, pruning exceptions, and accuracy–sparsity tradeoffs. Much of v1's knowledge-preservation interpretation of fine-tuning is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a repository link, LXT implementation information, seed-setting code, dataset-generation recipes, and detailed pruning instructions in Appendix A.6. Hardware descriptions are largely retained. Reproducibility documentation expands substantially, although A.6.3 specifies ResNet-32 while the corresponding figures label ResNet-34.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated related-work section with substantive comparisons to BrainProp, neuron-level reinforcement, and explanation-guided training or gradient modification. It expands pruning and transformer-LRP references while removing v1's lottery-ticket and shattered-gradient positioning.

P1.justification: V2 expands the title and extensively rewrites the abstract and motivation, increasingly using 'reward' terminology. It introduces dedicated related work, reorganizes the method and applications, and replaces the conclusion with a Discussion containing separate Strengths and Limitations and Future Work subsections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as a forward/reward/update workflow. V2 adds a capabilities diagram and configuration, reward, and accuracy tables. Experimental displays are redesigned around decision boundaries, weight/Gini plots, and multi-criterion pruning panels; SNN epoch curves become learning-rate plots. Appendix figures are extensively replaced and expanded.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the theoretical and empirical foundation: Appendix A.2 replaces v1's approximate sign argument with an inductive gradient-equivalence derivation, while Table 3 and expanded pruning studies test broader applicability and expose failure cases. Clearer limitations and implementation documentation further improve assessability. Removed fine-tuning/depth analyses and the model-naming inconsistency are drawbacks, but the gains in evidential support and clarity are substantial.
